scope: Implementation inventory for the current source. Passing qualification results are recorded separately.

interface_and_execution.interface: Unsupported GNU syntax is passed to the original GNU invocation; accepting that interface does not mean fd executes every feature.
interface_and_execution.execution: fd_listing, fd_gnu_evaluation and fd_incremental_control count as fd contribution only when an actual directory query supplies used descendant records. Root-only prune/quit, scan-free roots, original GNU actions and discarded queries receive no fd credit.

required: At least one successful fd directory query contributes candidate records to the result
GNU does not recursively rewalk the original invocation
excluded: A plan whose backend field is fd without an actual directory query
An incidental fd invocation whose records are discarded before whole-call GNU fallback
A file-only starting-point invocation with no directory traversal
GNU informational or validation-only invocations with no input search
Root-only output supplied by starting-path metadata when fd returns no contributing descendant records
acceleration_definition.performance: fd supplies traversal; this does not guarantee a speedup for every expression or filesystem.

routes.fd_listing: fd supplies candidates; the bounded byte-safe expression evaluator restores GNU order and print effects.
routes.fd_gnu_evaluation: fd supplies candidates; GNU evaluates ordered paths nonrecursively using -files0-from on a reserved private descriptor and -maxdepth 0.
routes.native: GNU receives the original argv and inherited input/output. This route is compatible fallback, not fd acceleration.
routes.fd_incremental_control: GNU evaluates each physical preorder entry through a persistent FIFO/PTY broker before fd enumerates its immediate children. Reached prune prevents that directory query; quit prevents later queries. Original expression truth, default print and output remain GNU-owned. Local GNU depth-one discovery can continue after fd failure without replaying prior expression output. Qualification requires a leading finite -maxdepth and a worst-case path-byte bound below Linux PATH_MAX; unbounded controls retain original GNU before output.

features.reason: Original GNU invocation owns its diagnostics and status.

printf_directives.rule: GNU's installed version validates each format. Unsupported directives retain GNU diagnostics; split requests with parse warnings use native GNU.
printf_directives.access_time: a and A require regular-file-only output conditions.
printf_directives.tty: Contextual d/H/P formats use native GNU when stdout is a terminal.

boundaries.native_when: Outside Linux, unavailable cwd, or failed current-directory /proc qualification.
boundaries.requirements: Supported operation requires usable GNU find, fd or fdfind, and Linux /proc; GNU evaluator dependency validation fails before fd enumeration.

boundaries.native_when: Public Bash/private function detect invalid UTF-8 argv bytes; raw argv is forwarded before Node decoding. Valid Unicode is eligible.
Current directory contains invalid UTF-8 bytes or its pathname has been removed.
Unnormalized starting paths, failed root lookup, or more than 256 roots.
boundaries.note: File/symlink roots may be evaluated without a directory query and do not count as traversal acceleration.

boundaries.native_when: A path/ipath/wholename/iwholename pattern ends in slash, because GNU warnings depend on original roots.
-H uses a symbolic-link reference operand requiring different original-root and descendant reference policy.
A contextual printf or -H split would repeat GNU parse warnings.
Access-time predicates (-amin/-atime/-anewer/-used or -neweraX) or printf a/A can produce output for directories or symlinks.
boundaries.note: fd and ordering reads may update access times. The output-condition summary must prove only regular files can produce output. The incremental physical control route evaluates entries before their own descent and keeps references in one GNU parse; buffered routes retain the stated access-time guard.

boundaries.native_when: An access-time reference operand (-newerXa) names a directory or symbolic link.
boundaries.note: The incremental physical control route evaluates entries before their own descent and keeps references in one GNU parse; buffered routes retain the stated access-time guard.

boundaries.native_when: Explicit access-time guards apply.
boundaries.note: A buffered traversal evaluates relative clock predicates later than native traversal. Concurrent filesystem mutation and exact boundary-crossing clock equivalence are not guaranteed.

boundaries.native_when: Traversal globals occur after expression primaries.
Depth is not decimal digits, exceeds 1000000, or its lexical length exceeds 10.
Expression exceeds 256 nodes or nesting/unary depth exceeds 64.
A GNU predicate/format argument exceeds 8192 bytes.
fd/fdfind is unavailable, emits stderr, exits unsuccessfully, times out, exceeds capture bounds, or returns malformed/escaped/duplicate candidate records.
boundaries.note: fdfind is tried only when fd is absent. Incremental control preparation also requires util-linux script, mkfifo and a safe private scratch directory outside all traversed roots. Preparation failure runs original GNU before output; failure during a directory query uses only local GNU depth-one discovery without replaying earlier expressions.

boundaries.native_when: A needed ordering parent has more than 10000 entries, ordering requires more than 10000 parent directories or 200000 total entries, or entries change during ordering.
A public Bash or private shell-function entry point detects closed caller stdin, stdout or stderr before Node startup.
boundaries.note: Node can reopen missing standard descriptors to /dev/null. Direct GNU dispatch preserves original closed-descriptor diagnostics and status.

boundaries.native_when: fd candidates exceed 100000 or captured bytes exceed 33554432.
The in-process listing result exceeds 100000 output records or 33554432 output bytes.
boundaries.note: GNU evaluator stdout is inherited; arbitrary GNU formatting output is not buffered under this listing-output limit.

boundaries.native_when: A GNU input list, contextual rewrite, or grouped evaluator arguments exceed bounded limits before output.
The in-process listing route uses -print with terminal stdout.
Contextual printf is used with terminal stdout.
Logical dereferencing and a detected cross-filesystem directory require GNU boundary evaluation.
Incremental controls lack a leading finite -maxdepth, or worst-case displayed/absolute paths can reach Linux PATH_MAX.
boundaries.note: Native GNU FTS can traverse beyond PATH_MAX using directory anchors. A files0 maxdepth-zero broker cannot represent those paths independently. This boundary is decided before broker output; a reproduced >4096-byte descendant tree is retained as an independent regression.

nonprewalkable_counterexamples.native_behavior: The skip directory is never descended into.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.prewalk_problem: A buffered fd walk has already visited the excluded tree. Even discarded candidates can change directory access times or trigger inaccessible-tree errors. Calling that discarded traversal acceleration would misstate execution.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.current_resolution: Eligible pure physical preorder controls with a finite-depth/path-byte proof use the incremental GNU decision/fd child-listing route. Unbounded or unsupported controls retain original GNU; buffered prewalking remains unsuitable.

nonprewalkable_counterexamples.native_behavior: GNU prints the starting root and stops before reading later descendants.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.prewalk_problem: Enumerating the entire tree before evaluation performs reads that the original command never performs.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.current_resolution: Eligible pure physical preorder controls with a finite-depth/path-byte proof use the incremental GNU decision/fd child-listing route. Unbounded or unsupported controls retain original GNU; buffered prewalking remains unsuitable.

nonprewalkable_counterexamples.native_behavior: A new file created while evaluating the root is included when GNU subsequently enumerates that directory.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.prewalk_problem: A previously buffered candidate list omits the new file.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.evidence: An owned synthetic GNU probe printed both the initial keep file and newly created new file with status zero.

nonprewalkable_counterexamples.native_behavior: A victim removed while evaluating the root is absent from the later directory enumeration.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.prewalk_problem: A previously buffered candidate list still contains the removed path and can produce wrong output or errors.
nonprewalkable_counterexamples.evidence: An owned synthetic GNU probe printed only the untouched keep file with status zero and no stderr.

cancellation: SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP stop owned fd process groups and native evaluator descendants; cleanup is scoped and does not claim containment of arbitrary escaped daemons.

known_compatibility_gaps.status: fixed for public Bash and private shell-function entry points; direct Node API requires explicit low-descriptor context
known_compatibility_gaps.reproduction: The original low-fd3 native -exec regression is covered by the new caller descriptor snapshot and inheritance helper.
known_compatibility_gaps.impact: Public Bash and private shell-function entry points snapshot descriptors before Node startup changes close-on-exec flags. Direct Node API callers must supply callerDescriptors for low descriptors when no launch snapshot is available. High non-CLOEXEC caller descriptors are discovered without an arbitrary descriptor-number cap.

documented_option_inventory.count_meaning: Finite representative spellings and routes, not exhaustive values or proof that every qualified representative completes with contributing fd traversal.

incremental_path_qualification.proof: Leading finite maxdepth times256 plus displayed, absolute and canonical root bytes must fit4095 bytes. statfs and bounded mountinfo reject unknown root or nested filesystem types before output.
incremental_path_qualification.limitations: The mount/filesystem checks are not a filesystem snapshot; arbitrary concurrent mount changes are not universally proved. CIFS/FUSE/overlay are not qualified by this route.

routing_policy.default: Direct original GNU before Node/preflight; normal Pi Bash remains unchanged.
routing_policy.reason: Current semantically qualified fd routes do not establish a universal wall-time win; no automatic fd forcing.
routing_policy.verification: Explicitly enable experimental semantic routes and independently require native default CLI/API/private/Pi behavior.
